diagnostic_evidence.quote: Some of these problems are extremely difficult - in the Appendix, we give an example where determining whether a system is ergodic has $\mathrm{SCI}=\infty$.

issues.failure_explanation: The Discussion asserts that the Appendix contains an example where deciding ergodicity has SCI=infinity. The only SCI=infinity result in the Appendix is thm:rotation(c), which concerns computing the spectrum of non-continuous measure-preserving invertible circle maps; it does not analyze the SCI of determining ergodicity. The claimed example is therefore absent and the sentence is unsupported.

issues.title: Discussion claims an appendix example of ergodicity with SCI=infinity that does not exist

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \Omega_{\mathcal{X}}=\left\{F:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{X}\text{ such that $F$ is continuous and non-singular, $\mathcal{K}_F$ is bounded}\right\},

issues.failure_explanation: The class Omega_X^m is defined as all measure-preserving maps, with no continuity requirement, while Omega_X requires continuity. Hence Omega_X^m is not a subset of Omega_X, so the proof's reduction to the continuous case is invalid. Moreover, thm:rotation(c) shows that dropping continuity on the circle makes the SCI infinite for the spectrum; for the unitary Koopman operators there spec=spec_ap, so the claimed Sigma_2^G classification for Omega_X^m is false as stated.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add continuity to the definition of Omega_X^m in both the appendix and the main text, restricting the theorem to continuous measure-preserving maps. This preserves the result for the intended class.
issues.overall_effect: The classification {Xi_ap,Omega_X^m} in Sigma_2^G and the main-text thm2 claim 'Two limits for Omega_X^m' are unsupported for discontinuous measure-preserving maps. The summary bullet 'SCI of computing the spectrum of measure-preserving systems is <=2' is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that $C(\{c_i\})$ is a shift operator on $\{e_i:c_i=1\}$ and zero on the span of the other basis elements.

If $\sum_{i=1}^\infty a_{i,j}=+\infty$, the operator $C(\{c^{(j)}_i\})$ is unitarily equivalent to the direct sum of a zero operator and the bilateral shift operator on $l^2(\mathbb{Z})$. Otherwise, it is unitarily equivalent to the direct sum of a zero operator and a shift operator acting on a finite-dimensional invariant subspace of dimension at least $2j+1$.

issues.failure_explanation: A shift operator on a finite-dimensional space is nilpotent and has spectrum {0}, not the unit disk. Thus for Q(a)=0, where infinitely many columns have only finitely many 1's, A(a) is a direct sum of finite nilpotent shifts and has spectrum {0}, not the unit disk. The embedding then gives dist(1/2,spec)=1/2 for both Q=1 (spectrum T) and Q=0 (spectrum {0}), so the algorithm cannot recover Q. The claimed lower bound SCI>=3 is unproven.

failure_location.quote: Otherwise, for any $N\in\mathbb{N}$, there is a finite-dimensional invariant subspace of dimension at least $N$ upon which $A(a)$ acts as a shift operator. Hence, $\spec(A(a))$ is the complex unit disc in this case.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; a repair must construct a different embedding or a different combinatorial problem whose spectra distinguish the two cases, e.g., producing the unit disk for the Q=0 case or choosing a different test point.
issues.overall_effect: The lower bound in thm:discrete_space is invalid, so the main-text thm3 claim that learning spec_ap for Omega_N has SCI=3 and requires three limits is unsupported. Only the Pi_3 upper bound survives.
issues.title: Lower bound in thm:discrete_space uses a false spectral claim about finite shifts
